IDA named publicly among the FFRDCs the congressional UAP inquiry is examining

claims.text: Adm. Charles A. Richard, USN (Ret.), is President of the Institute for Defense Analyses, having commanded US Strategic Command from 2019 to 2022.

IDA's senior leadership includes former NSA Technical Director Christopher Green (VP, Center for Communications and Computing) and Maj. Gen. James R. Marrs, USAF (Ret.), former National Intelligence Manager for Aviation.

IDA is among the federally funded research organisations named in public reporting on the congressional UAP contractor inquiry, alongside MIT Lincoln Laboratory, MITRE, RAND, the Aerospace Corporation, JPL and Sandia.

label: Charles A. Richard
narrative: Richard commanded United States Strategic Command from 2019 to 2022 - global command and control of every US strategic nuclear force - and now runs the Institute for Defense Analyses, the FFRDC operator whose Systems and Analyses Center answers to the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment and whose Center for Communications and Computing answers to the National Security Agency. His IDA leadership bench continues the pattern: Maj. Gen. James R. Marrs (Ret.), formerly Assistant Deputy Chief of Staff for ISR and National Intelligence Manager for Aviation; Christopher Green, formerly NSA Technical Director for the Engagement and Policy Directorate; Laura Baldwin, formerly associate director of RAND's National Security Research Division. IDA matters to this domain for two reasons. First, it was the original administrator of JASON from 1960 until 1973, before the contract went to SRI International and eventually to MITRE - meaning the government's most sensitive standing scientific advisory panel has spent its entire existence housed inside one FFRDC operator or another, never inside the government. Second, Rep. Burlison and NewsNation have both named IDA among the FFRDCs the congressional UAP inquiry is following. His tenure as STRATCOM commander overlaps exactly with the UAP Task Force period and the standing-up of AARO.
